---
title: "Selection and evaluation using posterior draws"
subtitle: "2.18 · after the postrank vignette m6 and theory book, chapter 21"
description: "Discrepancy between risk estimated on selection draws and risk under the exact posterior law."
---

Each repetition selects a report on posterior draws and scores that fixed report twice: on those selection draws and under the exact law.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Own draws.** “33 look worse” (33–37 across ties); Run 1's gap is −.000613.
- **Looks worse.** Run 6 minimizes own-draw risk yet has gap +.000720.
- **More draws.** At 4,000 draws, Run 1's gap narrows to −.000246.
- **Tighter family.** Across 603 reports (at most three grades), Run 1's gap is +.00102.
- **Both scores.** Equal-weight scores A and B give gap −.00322.

<details>
<summary>Bounds, regret and fold evaluation</summary>

Gray intervals bound the absolute difference between the two risk evaluations for each selected report, while regret compares that report's exact-law risk with the exact-law minimum. The example uses independent draws from normal posteriors for six fictional sites; the separate package fold example selects on one half of posterior draws and evaluates on the other, so it does not test performance on new observations.
</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
cf <- postrank_crossfit(postrank_toy, settings=postrank_settings(weights=c(need_A=.6,need_B=.4),tau=.25,G_max=3L), backend="highs")
cf[c("mean_optimism", "mean_abs_optimism")]
```
This reproduces the separate package fold example, not the browser's six-site draws.
:::

Standalone: [open the app](../../embed/chosen-and-judged.html), for example `?S=100&seed=1&run=6`.
